newsitem.title: GERMANY: ATHLETICS-COUNTRIES NOT SENDING STARS COULD BE FINED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-COUNTRIES NOT SENDING STARS COULD BE FINED.

text.p: Carl Olaf Homen, president of the European Athletic Association (EAA), said on Friday that members unable to persuade their best athletes to compete in the European Cup could be fined.
"We are considering ways of financially forcing countries to send their best teams," Homen said on the eve of the weekend's European Cup.
"The EAA pays quite a large travel subsidy and accommodation and we are looking at ways of reducing the cost."

Most of the competing nations' top athletes are in Munich. But some, such as Ukrainian shot putter Vita Pavlysh who was fourth at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, have decided to miss the event in order to concentrate on preparing for the world championships in August in Athens.
Homen also hinted that the EAA may make the European Cup a two-yearly event again.
The competition has been held annually since 1993 but it has been far from successful in its new format with poor crowds in 1995 in Lille, France, and last year in Madrid.

"When we turned the European Cup into an annual competition there was the general feeling that there needed to be a team competition every year," Homen said."A few countries are now saying we should reconsider."
"There are far too many championships in a four-year cycle," said Malcolm Arnold, the British head coach. "There are going to be a lot of tired athletes at the end of this year."
